mod.serving.name: vLLM: execution and operation
mod.serving.desc: From a scheduled batch to generated tokens, reliable requests and measured service quality.
mod.serving.lead: Scheduling makes a batch. Execution computes its outputs; operation keeps the service useful under real traffic.
mod.serving.goal.1: Connect the model runner, sampling and parallel execution.
mod.serving.goal.3: Reason about latency, failures and safe resource limits.
mod.serving.key.1: A serving system manages many users, not just a model: throughput, latency and resource limits must be considered together.
mod.11.key.1: Model behaviour comes from learned weights; activations carry the current sequence through shared computations.
mod.11.key.2: A cache avoids recomputing earlier K/V, but attention still reads a growing context.
mod.11.key.3: A useful system needs both quality checks and workload measurements; seeing a slide is not evidence of mastering it.
mod.4.key.6: Attention mixes information from available token positions using input-dependent weights.
mod.4.key.7: The MLP transforms each token separately; its output must fit the residual stream before addition.
mod.6.goal.4: distinguish pretraining, SFT, preference learning and low-rank adaptation
learning.lab.quality: Copy the quality fixtures and scoring client
learning.lab.quality.note: Save the first block as tasks.json and the second as lab-quality.py. These are visible teaching fixtures, not an independent held-out test. Use the same LAB_MAX_TOKENS and requested concurrency as the load client; the maximum simultaneous quality requests is limited by the number of tasks. Preserve answers and finish reasons, and evaluate representative responses under actual sustained load before claiming equal quality.
